{{Short description|Theorem in the large deviations theory of stochastic processes}}
In [[mathematics]], the '''Freidlin–Wentzell theorem''' (due to [[Mark Freidlin]] and [[Alexander D. Wentzell]]) is a result in the [[large deviations theory]] of [[stochastic process]]es.  Roughly speaking, the Freidlin–Wentzell theorem gives an estimate for the probability that a (scaled-down) sample path of an [[Itō diffusion]] will stray far from the mean path.  This statement is made precise using [[rate function]]s.  The Freidlin–Wentzell theorem generalizes [[Schilder's theorem]] for standard [[Brownian motion]].

==Statement==
Let ''B'' be a standard Brownian motion on '''R'''<sup>''d''</sup> starting at the origin, 0&nbsp;&isin;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>, and let ''X''<sup>''&epsilon;''</sup> be an '''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>-valued Itō diffusion solving an Itō [[stochastic differential equation]] of the form

:<math>\begin{cases} dX_t^\varepsilon = b(X_t^\varepsilon) \, dt + \sqrt{\varepsilon} \, dB_t, \\ X_0^\varepsilon = 0, \end{cases}</math>

where the drift [[vector field]] ''b''&nbsp;:&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup> is [[Lipschitz continuity|uniformly Lipschitz continuous]].  Then, on the [[Banach space]] ''C''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;=&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>([0,&nbsp;''T''];&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>) equipped with the [[supremum norm]] ||&sdot;||<sub>&infin;</sub>, the family of processes (''X''<sup>''&epsilon;''</sup>)<sub>''&epsilon;''&gt;0</sub> satisfies the large deviations principle with good rate function ''I''&nbsp;:&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>&nbsp;&rarr;&nbsp;'''R'''&nbsp;&cup;&nbsp;{+&infin;} given by

:<math>I(\omega) = \frac{1}{2} \int_0^T | \dot{\omega}_t - b(\omega_t) |^2 \, dt</math>

if ''&omega;'' lies in the [[Sobolev space]] ''H''<sup>1</sup>([0,&nbsp;''T''];&nbsp;'''R'''<sup>''d''</sup>), and ''I''(''&omega;'')&nbsp;=&nbsp;+&infin; otherwise.  In other words, for every [[open set]] ''G''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub> and every [[closed set]] ''F''&nbsp;&sube;&nbsp;''C''<sub>0</sub>,

:<math>\limsup_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \big( \varepsilon \log \mathbf{P} \big[ X^\varepsilon \in F \big]\big) \leq -\inf_{\omega \in F} I(\omega)</math>

and

:<math>\liminf_{\varepsilon \downarrow 0} \big( \varepsilon \log \mathbf{P} \big[ X^{\varepsilon} \in G \big]\big) \geq - \inf_{\omega \in G} I(\omega).</math>
